A1.justification: Both supplied PDFs contain the same SIFT paper, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–E. Pages 2–23 render identically; page 1 differs only in the arXiv version/date stamp and its placement.

before.justification: v1 reports original Wan and CogVideoX experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–3, component ablations in Table 4, and human evaluations in Fig. 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original quantitative comparisons, ablation results, qualitative examples, and human evaluations in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.5 and Algorithm 1 are identical. Self-imagination from noise, alternating R3D/SlowFast supervision, the auxiliary reconstruction loss, and progressive hard-case replay remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 4,000-video dataset and camera-only/object-only benchmark, together with the same multi-object, articulated-motion, and long-horizon evaluations in Sections 4.1–4.2.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the original Wan and CogVideoX models and their SFT variants, with VideoREPA evaluated on CogVideoX. Table 2 retains CameraCtrl and Wan-Move; no comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: The 100-prompt benchmark, 40-prompt ablation subset, 50 prompts per complex-motion setting, SA/PC metrics, training settings, and human-evaluation procedures are identical in Section 4 and Appendices A/C.

E4.justification: The reconstruction diagnostic in Fig. 2, component ablations in Table 4, classifier-training analysis in Fig. 7, and directional failure case in Appendix D/Fig. S2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same reporting of participant-averaged human scores and winning percentages in Appendix C. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, plotted curves, preference percentages, and qualitative findings match. For example, Wan+SIFT retains camera-only VLM SA/PC scores of 4.80/4.93 in Table 1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including diffusion/flow preliminaries, classification loss, replay schedule, and batch-loss formulation, are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about motion entanglement, reconstruction shortcuts, and SIFT's improvements to physical plausibility and motion disentanglement.

C2.justification: The interpretations of SFT performance, classifier overfitting, and replay remain unchanged. Both retain the four-class taxonomy and classifier-reliability limitations in Section 5, plus the directional-grounding explanation of failures in Appendix D.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A/C provide identical hardware, hyperparameters, prompt-generation instructions, evaluation prompts, and human-study details. Code/data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 71 references are unchanged, as is the positioning against simulation-driven, semantic-planning, and externally controlled video-generation approaches.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp text changes from v1, 26 Jun 2026, to v3, 4 Aug 2026. The title, authors, prose, section ordering, and appendix structure are identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes placement. All figures, tables, captions, and the remaining page layout are identical, including the appendices.

improvement.justification: The supplied later PDF preserves the same method, evidence, results, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information. Updating and repositioning the arXiv stamp does not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's scientific quality or readability.
